page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8y.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by Alibaba's custom arm64 Yitian YiTian710 processor, offering 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.75 GHz without hardware multithreading. It provides 128 GB of system memory, establishing a generous 8:1 memory-to-core allocation. The architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 64 MB L3 cache. Networking provides a 10 Gbps baseline, and the instance contains no local instance storage or bundled GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier capability across both compute and memory domains. The 16 dedicated cores produce a stress-ng multi-core score of 28,967.52 and a Passmark CPU rating of 12,775.06. Memory performance is characterized by an uncached 256 MB read bandwidth of 80.38 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 40.44 GB/sec, alongside a cached small-block read bandwidth of 1639.97 GB/sec. Data processing efficiency shows 14,714.33 operations on Passmark database tests and 25.52 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, reflecting solid operational throughput for memory-bound queues.

A noticeable architectural limitation appears in hardware cryptographic performance, where the Passmark CPU encryption test recorded a low-tier score of 2615.37. Additionally, processing prompts on larger 7B language models remains constrained at 21.14 tokens per second. Because the server lacks ephemeral local disk space, all storage operations depend entirely on network-attached volumes. Given its high RAM density per CPU core, the ecs.r8y.4xlarge offers favorable resource efficiency for in-memory data structures, Redis caching layers, relational database hosting, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8y.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by a 16-core arm64 Alibaba Yitian YiTian710 processor operating at 2.75 GHz with dedicated physical cores. It provides 128 GB of RAM, offering an 8 GB per vCPU ratio well matched to memory-bound enterprise services. The server features a 10 Gbps baseline network interface without bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations show solid mid-tier multi-core compute with 28,967.52 on stress-ng and 25.52 million Redis SET operations per second, supported by 80.38 GB/sec uncached read memory bandwidth. However, Passmark cryptographic scores and larger LLM prompt processing exhibit weaker comparative efficiency. Without internal storage drives, all persistence relies on remote block storage. The instance configuration is best aligned with in-memory caching clusters, relational database engines, and intermediate data processing workloads.
